verbose: Okay so before I go home, actually what I wanted to tell you is that the gentleman in bed four, his blood pressure was going up and down, up and down the whole night, so kindly check it every hour and inform the doctor if anything is happening.
reference: Bed four's blood pressure was erratic overnight — hourly obs, please, and escalate if it drops.

verbose: Just to update you, the lady in bay two is much better compared to yesterday, she is eating, she is walking also, but still she is not fully recovered, so we cannot say she is totally fine, but she is improving day by day.
reference: Bay two's on the mend — eating and walking — though not out of the woods yet.

verbose: I am having one small request regarding the rota, actually my brother's function is there on Saturday, so if possible can someone kindly exchange the night shift with me, I will do their shift on any other day, whichever day they are wanting.
reference: Could anyone swap my Saturday night shift? I'll do one of theirs in lieu.

verbose: What happened is that two of the nurses have phoned and told that they are not well, they are having fever, so they are not coming today, so we are very short of staff on the ward today, it is very difficult situation.
reference: Two nurses have called in sick, so we're badly short on the ward today.

verbose: So basically what I am trying to explain to you is that the doctor is busy right now with one emergency case, so she will come and see you, but it may take some more time, so please wait for some time and do not worry.
reference: I'm afraid the doctor's dealing with an emergency, but she'll see you soon. Thanks for your patience.

verbose: Kindly note that your operation date is not fixed yet, because the list is very long and many patients are there before you, so we will inform you when the date is coming, till then you have to wait only.
reference: You're on the waiting list, and we'll be in touch once there's a date.

verbose: I wanted to tell you that I have sent the letter to the hospital specialist for your knee problem, and now they will call you for the appointment, it can take some weeks, so if they are not calling in six weeks you please call us back.
reference: I've made the referral for your knee. If you've not heard in six weeks, give us a ring.

verbose: Regarding your medicine, actually the tablets you are asking for, those ones you can directly buy from any medical shop without the doctor's paper, there is no need to take a prescription for that, it is very simple medicine only.
reference: You don't need a prescription — you can get those over the counter at any chemist.

verbose: The thing is that today the hospital is completely full, there are no beds anywhere in any ward, and patients are waiting in the emergency department for many many hours, so we are not able to admit anybody more, the situation is very bad.
reference: We're at capacity — no beds anywhere, and A&E's backing up.

verbose: First of all I am extremely sorry, very very sorry, for what happened with your mother's appointment, it was our mistake only, the letter went to the old address, and we will make sure that this kind of thing will not happen again in future.
reference: I'm terribly sorry about your mother's appointment — the letter went to an old address. We'll put that right.

verbose: As you all know, the money for the extra physiotherapy staff was given only for one year, and after March month it is finishing, and we still don't know if they will give more money or not, nothing is confirmed from their side.
reference: Funding for the extra physio posts ends in March, and renewal's still up in the air.

verbose: Just a gentle reminder to everybody that the infection control audit forms have to be submitted by this Friday itself, kindly do the needful and complete all the forms properly, otherwise we will get into problem with the management.
reference: Just a quick reminder: infection control audits are due on Friday.

verbose: Actually our regular doctor is on leave for two weeks, she has gone out of station, so one temporary doctor will be coming in her place, so the patients may see a new face, but he is also fully qualified, no issue at all.
reference: Our GP's away for a fortnight, so a locum's covering — fully qualified, of course.

verbose: I wanted to discuss about one thing with you, I am feeling that I am not getting enough chance to do the procedures by myself, always the senior is doing it, so I am not learning properly, can you please help me in this matter.
reference: Can I have a quick word? I'd like to do more procedures myself — I'm mostly observing.
targets: can I have a quick word?

verbose: Your presentation was very good, I liked it very much, only one small thing is that the slides were having too much text, too much writing, so people were busy reading and not listening to you, otherwise everything was perfect.
reference: Great presentation. Just a thought: fewer words on the slides would keep people listening.

verbose: I am requesting you to kindly sanction my leave for the second week of next month, because there is a family wedding in my native place, and I have already informed earlier also, so please approve it at the earliest possible.
reference: Could I book annual leave for the second week of next month? There's a family wedding.

verbose: Basically the computer system is not working since morning, we are not able to see any patient records or the test results, the IT people are saying they are working on it but they are not giving any time when it will come back.
reference: The records system's been down since this morning, and IT can't give us a timescale.

verbose: So the operation in theatre two is taking much longer than what we were expecting, there were some complications, so the afternoon patients will have to wait more or maybe their surgery will be shifted to some other day.
reference: Theatre two has overrun, so this afternoon's list may move to another day.

verbose: Your father is medically fit to go home now, but the problem is that the care at home is not arranged yet, the social services people are still working on it, so till that is done he will have to stay in the hospital only.
reference: Your father's ready to go home; the bottleneck is his care package, which isn't in place yet.

verbose: Actually we were thinking that maybe your mother needs more support than what can be given at home, so the best option may be to move her to some place where nurses are there all the time, but it is your decision only.
reference: We think a care home might suit your mother better — but it's entirely your decision.

verbose: Before we finish the meeting, is there anything else anybody wants to discuss, any other point or any issue, which we have not covered so far, then please tell now itself, otherwise we can close the meeting and go.
reference: Any other business before we wrap up?

verbose: So who will be writing down what all we are discussing today in the meeting, because last time nobody wrote anything and later everyone was confused about what we decided and who will be doing what work.
reference: Could someone take the minutes? Last time nobody was sure what we'd agreed.

verbose: I tried to call the doctor three times regarding the patient's high temperature, but nobody is picking up the phone, so I am not knowing what to do now, should I call someone senior or just keep on waiting for the doctor.
reference: I've bleeped the doctor three times with no answer, so I'll escalate to the registrar.

verbose: There is one new training module that all the staff members are supposed to complete, it is online only, it takes around one hour, and the last date for completing it is end of this month, so please everybody finish it.
reference: There's a new hour-long compliance module for everyone, due by the end of the month.

verbose: For the new nurses who are joining from next week, someone has to show them around the ward, explain all the systems and rules and everything, and stay with them for first few days so they understand how we are doing things here.
reference: Could someone buddy the new nurses next week and help them learn the ropes?

verbose: If you are needing a letter for your office saying that you are not well and cannot work, then for the first seven days you can just write it yourself, after that only the doctor will give the official letter for you.
reference: You can self-certify for seven days; after that, the GP can give you a sick note.

verbose: If at night time the pain is becoming very bad and you are not able to bear it, and it is not a big emergency, then don't directly go to hospital, first call the number one-one-one and they will guide you what to do.
reference: If the pain gets worse overnight and it's not an emergency, ring 111 for advice.

verbose: Actually for this small chest cold you don't need to wait for the doctor's appointment, you can directly go and talk to the medical shop person, they are also trained, they will tell you which medicine to take, it will save your time.
reference: For a chesty cold, the pharmacist can advise you — no need to wait for an appointment.

verbose: So one lady from the health side will come to your house after the baby is born, she will check the baby's weight and how the feeding is going and all that, and she will also answer any questions you are having.
reference: A health visitor will pop round after the birth to check the baby's weight and feeding.

verbose: I am calling to tell you that your appointment with the pregnancy nurse which was on Tuesday, that is now shifted to Thursday same time, because she is having some training on Tuesday, sorry for the trouble caused to you.
reference: Your midwife appointment's moved from Tuesday to Thursday, same time — apologies.

verbose: Good news is there, one cancellation happened in the clinic, so if you are free, we can give you the appointment next Monday itself instead of waiting till end of next month, should I go ahead and book it for you?
reference: We've had a cancellation, so we can bring your appointment forward to Monday. Shall I book it?

verbose: Kindly be informed that this is not an admission, you will come in the morning, the doctor will see you and do some tests, and same day evening you can go back home, you need not stay overnight in the hospital.
reference: It's an outpatient appointment — you'll be home the same day.

verbose: The senior doctor who is in charge of your treatment, the main specialist, he wants to see you personally next week to discuss about the results and what are the next steps, so please don't miss that appointment.
reference: Your consultant would like to see you next week to talk through the results.

verbose: I am very sorry to say this but the store room is in a very bad condition, things are lying here and there, nobody is keeping anything in proper place, and if the inspection people come they will make big issue out of it.
reference: The store room's in a state. Could we tidy it up before any inspection?

verbose: We are really struggling with staff on the night shifts since last two months, every night we are one or two nurses less than what is required, and people are getting very tired, I think something has to be done about this.
reference: Nights have been short-staffed for months and people are worn out. Can we look into it?

verbose: I noticed one thing, please don't mind, but in your notes you are not writing the time and signing properly every time, and that can create big problem if any complaint comes later, so please be careful about that thing.
reference: For what it's worth, do time and sign every entry — it matters if there's ever a complaint.

verbose: All of you please make sure that you have done the safeguarding training refresher, because the certificate is valid for only three years, and many people's certificates are expiring now, HR has sent the full list to me.
reference: HR have flagged up that several safeguarding certificates are lapsing — please check yours.

verbose: I have been trying since one week to get the access for the new prescribing system, I have sent many emails also, but nobody is replying me, so please can you help me in getting this done quickly as it is affecting my work.
reference: I've been waiting a week for prescribing system access. Could you help expedite it?

verbose: Since you are new and this is your first placement, don't feel shy, if any doubt is coming, any small doubt also, just ask me directly, no problem at all, I am here only to help you with everything.
reference: It's your first placement, so ask me anything — no question's too small. Happy to help.

verbose: Before the operation, you should not eat anything after twelve o'clock in the night, nothing at all, not even a small biscuit, but water you can drink till six in the morning, after that nothing please, not even water.
reference: Nothing to eat after midnight, and only water until six. Does that make sense?

verbose: If you have just shifted to this area, then the first thing you have to do is go to the nearby clinic and fill the form to become their patient, then only you can take appointments with the doctor there.
reference: Now you've moved, you'll need to register with a GP before you can book appointments.

verbose: The good news is that your blood test results have come back and everything is normal only, there is nothing to worry, the doctor has seen it and said no further tests are required, so you can relax now.
reference: Good news: your bloods are normal, so we can rule out anything serious.

verbose: I understand you are worried, but the ambulance people have told that all the vehicles are busy right now with other emergencies, so it will take maybe forty-five minutes more to reach, please stay with the patient till then.
reference: The ambulance is about forty-five minutes away, so please stay with them until the paramedics arrive.

verbose: The business case for the new scanner has to be submitted to the board by the end of this month, but the finance team has still not given the cost figures, so I am worried we will not be able to finish it on time.
reference: The scanner business case is due this month and finance's figures haven't come — it'll go down to the wire.

verbose: We wanted to buy new beds for the ward, but they are saying that we have to follow the proper buying process, take three quotations from different companies and all that, so it will take more time than we thought.
reference: The new beds have to go through procurement, so it'll take longer than expected.

verbose: So the audit results have come and overall we have done well, but in the hand hygiene part our score was little bit less than the target, so we need to improve in that area, rest everything was fine.
reference: The audit went well overall, but hand hygiene fell just short — there's room for improvement there.

verbose: The patient in room six is not able to speak or understand English properly, she is only comfortable in her own language, so for the consent discussion we will need someone who can translate properly, otherwise it will not be right.
reference: Room six needs an interpreter for consent — her understanding is paramount.

verbose: One important thing I forgot to tell, the antibiotics for bed nine, the evening dose was not given because the medicine was not available in pharmacy, they said they will send it, so please follow it up and make sure it is given.
reference: Bed nine missed the evening antibiotics — pharmacy were out. Could you chase it up?

verbose: Every month the rota is coming very late, just one or two days before the month is starting, and because of that we are not able to plan anything for our family or personal work, it is creating a lot of problem for everybody.
reference: The rota's published so late that nobody can plan around it — it's not ideal.

verbose: Tomorrow I have a hospital appointment for myself in the morning, so I will come little late, around eleven o'clock, so can somebody please manage my patients till I come, I will take over once I arrive there.
reference: I've an appointment tomorrow morning — could someone hold the fort until I'm in at eleven?

verbose: See, the management has decided that from next month we are changing from eight-hour shifts to twelve-hour shifts, so the timings will be different, and they are saying it is final, but nobody asked the staff opinion before deciding.
reference: We're moving to twelve-hour shifts next month, and staff weren't consulted — buy-in will be a problem.

verbose: Honestly speaking, getting the agency nurses for weekends is becoming very very difficult nowadays, many times we call and they say nobody is available, and even when they come, they are not knowing our ward at all.
reference: Weekend agency nurses are like gold dust, and they don't know the ward.

verbose: Regarding the complaint letter which the family has sent about the long waiting time in the clinic, we need to send them the reply within twenty working days, so kindly give me your statement by this week end itself.
reference: Could I have your statement on the clinic-wait complaint by Friday? We've twenty working days to reply.

verbose: I know we are running very late in this meeting, and still four more items are left on the list, so maybe we can quickly finish the important ones today and keep the remaining ones for the next meeting, what do you all think?
reference: I'm conscious of time, so shall we take the urgent items and defer the rest?

verbose: What we have been told is that the budget for the next year is going to be reduced by some amount, and every department has to save money, but they have not told exactly how much, so we cannot plan anything properly.
reference: Budgets are being trimmed next year, but without a ballpark figure we can't plan.

verbose: Please do not take tension, the result of the scan will come in two to three days only, and as soon as it comes the doctor will check it and we will call you directly, you need not call us again and again for that.
reference: The scan results should be back in a few days. Leave it with me — we'll ring you.

verbose: Actually this particular medicine is not available with us right now, the supplier is having some shortage problem from last few weeks, so I can give you half the quantity today and remaining you can collect next week.
reference: I'm afraid there's a national shortage, so it's half today and the rest next week.

verbose: Sorry for keeping you waiting so long on the phone, actually today the phone lines are very very busy since eight o'clock morning, everybody is calling for appointments at the same time, so it is taking time.
reference: Sorry to keep you waiting — the lines have been chock-a-block since eight.

verbose: For this kind of small cut you need not go to the big hospital emergency, there is another centre nearby which is open till late night, they can see you there and the waiting time will be much less also.
reference: For a minor cut, try the urgent treatment centre — it's open late and the wait's much shorter.

verbose: I want to give you some feedback, basically your clinical skills are very good, no doubt, but sometimes you are speaking with the patients very fast and using medical words, so they are not understanding what you are saying.
reference: Your clinical skills are strong. You might want to slow down and avoid jargon with patients.

verbose: When you were explaining to the family about the diagnosis, the way you handled the situation, very calm, very patient, giving them time for questions, honestly I learned a lot from watching you, you did a very good job.
reference: The way you broke that news was so calm and patient — I learned a lot. Well done.

verbose: I wanted to ask you whether it is possible that I can do the advanced course in wound care which is happening next term, because I am very interested in that area and I think it will be useful for our ward also.
reference: Would it be possible to do the wound care course next term? It'd really benefit the ward.

verbose: I am finding it very difficult to manage the school pickup with the current timings, so I was thinking if there is any option where I can start early and finish early, like seven to three, instead of the normal timings.
reference: Could I discuss flexitime? Seven till three would make the school run manageable.

verbose: The new admission in side room one, his tests are all sent, but results are still pending, so we are not sure what is the exact problem, the doctors also are thinking two three different possibilities, nothing is final yet.
reference: Side room one's bloods are pending, and the diagnosis is provisional for now.

verbose: I just want to tell you clearly that the patient in bay four, her condition is very serious, honestly it can go either way tonight, so please keep checking on her regularly and call the doctor immediately if anything changes.
reference: Bay four is touch and go tonight — check her often and call the doctor if anything changes.

verbose: One problem has come in the theatre this morning, the main machine for anaesthesia is not working properly, so the engineers are checking it, and until that is fixed we cannot start any operation, the whole list is getting delayed.
reference: An anaesthetic machine fault has thrown a spanner in the works — the whole list is delayed.

verbose: Before your surgery, the doctor who will give you the medicine to make you sleep will come and meet you, he will ask some questions about your health and allergies and all, so please tell him everything honestly.
reference: The anaesthetist will pop in before surgery to ask about your health and any allergies.

verbose: I am not fully agreeing with this idea of closing the minor injuries unit at weekends, because many people are using it, and if it is closed then they will all come to the main emergency, and that will become even more crowded.
reference: I have some reservations: closing minor injuries at weekends would have a knock-on effect on A&E.

verbose: The money which was given specially for the mental health support project should be used only for that purpose, it should not be taken and used for other things in the department, otherwise the project will not survive.
reference: The mental health project funding must be ring-fenced, or the project won't survive.

verbose: There is some mismatch between the number of patients in the computer system and the actual number of patients on the ward, the numbers are not matching, so somebody needs to check and correct it before the night report.
reference: There's a discrepancy between the system and the ward headcount — could someone reconcile it before nights?

verbose: I fully understand that you are angry and upset about the waiting time today, and you have every right to feel like that, and I am not making any excuses, but I would like to explain what happened, if you will allow me.
reference: I completely understand your frustration, and I won't make excuses. If I may, I'll explain what happened.

verbose: Okay so to quickly summarise everything which we discussed in the last one hour, the main points were the new rota, the staffing problem, and the audit results, and everybody knows what they have to do now, I hope so.
reference: To recap: the rota, staffing and the audit. Everyone's clear on their actions.

verbose: The report which the commissioners have asked for, they wanted it by next Wednesday, but now suddenly they are saying they want it by this Friday itself, so we have only three days now and lot of data is still missing.
reference: The commissioners now want the report by Friday — a tall order with data still missing.

verbose: Today the visits list is very long, there are fourteen patients to see in different villages, and two of our team members are on leave, so I don't think we will be able to finish all visits today, some may have to wait.
reference: Fourteen visits and two people down — we'll have to prioritise and push some back to tomorrow.

verbose: If you are getting any of these side effects like rash or swelling or feeling very dizzy after taking the tablets, then immediately stop taking them and contact us, don't wait thinking it will become okay on its own.
reference: If you get a rash, swelling or dizziness, stop the tablets and ring us straight away.

verbose: I have been working in this ward for almost three years now, and I am thinking I am ready for the next level, so I wanted to know if there is any chance of going for the senior nurse post when it comes.
reference: After three years, I'd like to go for the senior post. Could we discuss it at my appraisal?

verbose: Just to let all the outpatients know in advance, on the coming Tuesday and Wednesday some of the doctors will not be working because of the strike, so some clinics will be cancelled and we will call those patients individually.
reference: Some clinics will be cancelled next Tuesday and Wednesday due to industrial action; we'll contact those affected.

verbose: Kindly note that I will not be able to do the Sunday shift this week, because my child is having very high fever since yesterday and there is nobody else at home to take care of her, sorry for the late information.
reference: Sorry for the short notice — my daughter's poorly. Could someone stand in for me on Sunday?

verbose: So we did a small trial on one ward for two months where we gave patients a simple checklist when going home, and the results are looking good, readmissions came down, but it is only one ward so we cannot say for sure.
reference: Our discharge checklist pilot cut readmissions on one ward. Promising, but it's early days.

verbose: I am thinking if we can just change the way the morning medicine round is done, like we do the high-risk patients first, it will not cost anything, and it can reduce the mistakes quite a lot, it is very simple thing only.
reference: Doing high-risk patients first on the morning drug round would be a quick win — no cost, fewer errors.

verbose: Many patients are not coming for their appointments and they are also not informing us that they are not coming, so the doctor's time is getting wasted, and other patients who need the slot are not getting it.
reference: Unannounced no-shows are wasting slots — could we pilot text reminders?

verbose: You are doing so many extra shifts and also staying back late every day after your shift, I am little bit worried that you will get tired and fall sick, please take some rest also, your health is also important.
reference: You've done loads of extra shifts. Do take it easy, please.

verbose: I know you mean well, but the way you spoke to the junior nurse in front of everybody at the nurses' station, it was little bit harsh, she was feeling very bad afterwards, maybe next time you can talk to her separately.
reference: You meant well, but that was a bit public. It might be worth a quiet word next time.

verbose: We are getting so many referrals for the talking therapy service nowadays, the numbers have gone up so much, and we have the same number of therapists only, so the patients are waiting four to five months for their first session.
reference: Referrals have soared but therapist numbers haven't, so first sessions now take four or five months.

verbose: What we are planning is that from next month, for the routine appointments, first the patients will fill one online form, and then the team will decide whether they need to see the doctor or nurse or pharmacist, like that.
reference: From next month, routine requests start with an online form so we can streamline who sees whom.

verbose: After what happened today in the resuscitation room, I think it will be good if all of us sit together for ten minutes, just to talk about how everybody is feeling and what went well and what we can do better.
reference: After today in resus, shall we have a quick debrief — how everyone's doing, and what we'd change?

verbose: Good evening, actually I wanted to tell you that your son is a very bright boy, very intelligent, no doubt about that, but in the class he is talking too much with his friends and not concentrating, so his marks are coming down slowly.
reference: He's very bright, but chatting in class is starting to affect his marks.

verbose: So what I am trying to say is that your daughter is doing very well in all subjects, really very well, but in maths only she is struggling little bit, so if you can give some extra practice at home it will be very helpful.
reference: She's doing brilliantly overall; maths is the one area where a bit of practice at home would help.

verbose: I know there are many parents waiting outside for their turn, so I am not able to give you more time today, but if you want to discuss more about his progress, we can fix another meeting on some other day.
reference: I'm conscious of others waiting — shall we book another chat to go over his progress?

verbose: Tomorrow I will not be coming to school because I have to attend my cousin's wedding function, so I have prepared all the work for my classes, kindly arrange somebody to take my lessons and give the work to the children.
reference: I'm off tomorrow, so I've set work for all my classes. Could a supply teacher take them?

verbose: Kindly note that from next Monday the timetable is changing for Year Nine, the science lessons which were on Tuesday will now be on Thursday, and PE is moving to Tuesday, so please inform the students properly.
reference: Year 9's timetable changes on Monday: science moves to Thursday, PE to Tuesday.

verbose: The last date for submitting the coursework is this Friday only, after that the teachers cannot accept anything, because it has to be sent to the exam board for checking, so whoever has not finished, please finish it fast.
reference: Coursework's due Friday — no exceptions, as it goes to the exam board. Crack on!

verbose: During the examination, the people who are standing in the hall and watching the students, they need to make sure that no one is using the phone or talking, and if anything wrong is happening they should immediately report it.
reference: Invigilators must watch for phones or talking and report anything straight away.

verbose: For the students who failed in the English exam last summer, there is a chance to write the exam again in November, so please tell those students to register their names with the exams office before the end of this month.
reference: Students needing an English resit in November should sign up with the exams office this month.

verbose: The practice exams which we are having in January are very important, because based on those marks only the teachers will decide what grade to give for the university applications, so students should take them very seriously.
reference: January's mocks feed into predicted grades, so students need to take them seriously.

verbose: As you all know, on the first day after the holidays, the children will not be coming, only the teachers will come, and we will be having full-day training on the new behaviour policy, so please don't plan any leave on that day.
reference: The first day back is an INSET day on the new behaviour policy, so please don't book leave.

verbose: I am informing everybody that every morning the attendance must be taken within the first ten minutes of the first lesson, because the office is checking who is absent and calling the parents, and if it is late, the whole thing is delayed.
reference: Please take the register within ten minutes of first lesson so the office can ring parents.

verbose: Sir, I wanted to request one thing, I am having too many lessons this term, almost no free periods, and I am also doing the after-school club, so it is becoming very difficult for me to do marking and planning properly.
reference: With barely any free periods plus the club, I'm snowed under. Could we look at my timetable?

verbose: I observed your lesson yesterday and I really liked how you started with the small quiz, the children were very excited, but in the middle part you were talking for a long time, so some of them lost the interest.
reference: Lovely starter quiz. Engagement tailed off when you talked at length mid-lesson.

verbose: Basically your lesson planning is very good, very detailed, but I am thinking that maybe you are trying to cover too many things in one lesson, so the children are not getting time to practise what they learned.
reference: Your planning is thorough, but I'd be inclined to cover less so pupils get time to practise.

verbose: There is one boy in my Year Seven class who is needing extra support for reading, I think he may have some learning difficulty, so I wanted to know the proper process for getting him checked by the special needs team.
reference: A Year 7 boy may need reading support. How do I refer him to the SEND team?

verbose: The helper who is supporting in my class, she is very good, but she is spending all her time with only one table, so the other children who are also struggling are not getting any help from her side.
reference: Our teaching assistant is great, but she's tied to one table — others need support too.

verbose: If you are wanting admission for your child in this school, you have to check whether your house address is coming in the area which the school is covering, because preference is given to children living nearby only.
reference: Check you're in the catchment area — nearby families get priority.

verbose: Just to remind all the parents, the school will be closed for one week holiday from the twenty-third, and children will come back on the following Monday, and during this time the breakfast club will also not be running.
reference: School closes for half-term on the twenty-third; breakfast club is off too.

verbose: I am writing to you regarding the homework, actually my son is getting so much homework every night from all the subjects, he is sitting till ten-thirty at night to finish it, and he is not getting time to play or rest.
reference: My son's homework is keeping him up till half ten — it's a bit much.

verbose: Thank you for bringing this matter to my attention, I have spoken to all the teachers about the homework issue, and we have decided that we will make one proper schedule so that he does not get too much on the same night.
reference: Thanks for raising it. We'll set a homework timetable so no night is overloaded.

verbose: Tomorrow morning in the whole school gathering, one of the students from Year Eleven will be speaking about the charity run which they are doing, so the teachers please bring your form class to the hall by eight forty-five.
reference: Please bring your form to the hall by quarter to nine for tomorrow's assembly.

verbose: As your class teacher, the one who sees you every morning, I just want you to know that if you are having any problem, studies or friends or anything, you can come and talk to me anytime, my door is always open.
reference: As your form tutor, I'm always here if anything's bothering you.

verbose: For the students who are finishing Year Eleven and want to continue studying in our school for the next two years, the application forms are now available, and the last date is the end of January, so please apply early.
reference: Sixth form applications are open until the end of January — do apply early.

verbose: The essay which you write about yourself for the university form, you should not just list all your achievements one by one, you should explain why you are interested in the subject and what you did to explore it more.
reference: Your personal statement shouldn't just list achievements — show why the subject grips you.

verbose: If your final results are not good enough and the university you chose does not accept you, don't worry too much, there is a system in August where you can still find a place in other universities which have seats left.
